the artifact is 12 numbers. It uses no feature of the model other than the scheme label: not size, not family, not benchmark, not base accuracy. It is a lookup table.

an earlier version of this audit claimed the raw empirical band beats conformal (91.9% vs 90.3% here, with bands fitted in-sample on all training data). Under the STRICT protocol used elsewhere -- held-out calibration family, per scheme -- the ordering REVERSES: see src/interval_shape.py, conformal 89.0% at 3.93pp width vs empirical 88.3% at 5.48pp, on the 2306 rows where the empirical band is finite at all. The empirical band's apparent advantage came from returning +/-inf on 43% of rows, and an infinite interval always covers. Conformal stays.
0 of 6 scheme intervals exclude zero. The tool is STRUCTURALLY incapable of saying 'this config will cost you accuracy' -- for every scheme, 'no change' is inside the 90% interval.

gemma-3-1b-it W4A16 loses 1.88pp on average and misses the interval on 4 of 6 benchmarks (GSM8K -3.03, MMLU -2.99, ARC -2.90). The tool reports [-2.87, +1.40] and raises no warning. This is the limitation made concrete.

Qwen3-8B W4A16 on MMLU-Pro loses 8.86pp. The tool neither flags it nor covers it: a user would be told to expect about -0.73pp with a floor of -2.87pp, and would lose 8.9pp. This is the honest worst-case example to publish.
26 of 32 losses worse than 3pp fall below the interval floor. Large degradations are exactly where the envelope fails, and they are not rare: 32/1003 = 3.2% of all rows.

clustering does not materially widen the interval (11.0pp naive vs 11.5pp clustered); coverage misses are spread across models rather than concentrated in one, so the headline CI is not understating uncertainty
